summary: Hardens plugin lifecycle and secret-broker file reads against time-of-check/time-of-use races and removes an inefficient plugin-ID validation expression before the v0.14.0 release.
userImpact: Plugin lifecycle state, receipts, plans, credentials, and broker policy files are verified and read through the same non-symlink file descriptor.
Plugin installation and operation contracts remain compatible; no customer action is required beyond deploying the corrected v0.14.0 build.

instructions: Use the corrected v0.14.0 host and installer artifacts; do not publish or deploy the earlier unreleased candidate.

notes: This hardening changes no database schema or stored plugin data.

security: Uses descriptor-based bounded reads with O_NOFOLLOW so file type, size, and content are evaluated without a check-then-open race.
Replaces the ambiguous repeated plugin-ID regular expression with linear validation and explicit separator checks.
Documents the secret broker's intentional credential sink only after tenant-bound signed policy, HTTPS, method, path, timeout, response-size, redirect, and reflection controls are enforced.
Scopes missing-rate-limit suppressions to ephemeral loopback-only acceptance fixtures; production plugin routes remain protected by host gateway admission and rate limits.
documentation: Plugin platform security and trust boundaries: `docs/architecture/12-plugin-platform-and-authoring.md`
rollback: Redeploying the merged plugin-platform candidate would reintroduce the reported CodeQL findings; roll back the complete unreleased candidate rather than selectively reverting this hardening.
validation: Plugin installer and runtime unit, typecheck, lifecycle, multi-replica, and symlink-rejection suites
PR-scoped and merge-group CodeQL analysis with zero open alerts for the hardening PR
Full OSS PostgreSQL, Oracle, plugin-platform, package-boundary, image-smoke, and security gates
